meta.unit: The signs and the robber wars (3 Nephi 1–7)
principles: A government destroyed without a war
Kinship as the unit that survives
A ministry conducted among people who cannot deny it

world_behind.title: The king never happens
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says outright that they did not establish a king; they murdered the chief judge instead.

world_behind.title: The country reorganizes by family
world_behind.text: Verses 2 through 4 break the people into tribes drawn on family, kindred and friends, each with its own chief. Mosiah 29:25 to 32 had replaced kings with judges precisely to prevent this; the reign of the judges lasted ninety-one years and ends here.

world_behind.title: There is no war at this stage
world_behind.text: Verse 5 notes the collapse happened with no fighting among them.

world_behind.title: Six years is the span
world_behind.text: Verse 8 measures the fall from righteousness at under six years.

world_behind.title: The band gets its king and leaves
world_behind.text: Verses 9 through 13 have them naming Jacob king and marching north to build a kingdom and wait for dissenters.

world_behind.title: The tribes agree not to fight and still stone prophets
world_behind.text: Verse 14 has strict laws against trespass between tribes, some peace, and prophets stoned and cast out. Helaman 13:24 to 26 had charged the previous generation with exactly that treatment of prophets, so the political order changes completely and the treatment of messengers does not.

world_behind.title: Nephi's credentials are listed before his ministry
world_behind.text: Verse 15 names angels, the voice of the Lord, and eye-witness knowledge before the ministry begins. Helaman 10:4 to 11 records the grant of that authority, and 3 Nephi 1:12 the voice; the credential list is assembled from events the reader has watched.

words.text: Divisions of a people by descent. The record uses the word twenty times, usually of the tribes of Israel, and five of those uses are in this chapter of a Nephite political collapse.
What has been thrown up. The word occurs once in the record and eight times in the King James Bible. Verse 8 pairs it with the sow in the mire, the pairing 2 Peter 2:22 gives as a proverb.
Slowed or obstructed. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, of a march too fast to be stopped.
To encroach on what belongs to another. Treated at Mosiah 26:31. It appears once in the record, and eighty-two times in the King James Bible. Verse 14 uses it of one tribe against another.
One who saw a thing himself. Both of the record's uses are in this one verse, and the King James Bible has neither. Nephi is called an eye-witness twice, of different things.
Bodily weaknesses. Treated at Alma 7:12, where Christ takes them upon him. The record uses the word five times. Verse 22 has people healed of them testifying to what happened.

phrases.term: They did destroy upon the judgment-seat, yea, did murder the chief judge of the land
phrases.text: The end of the reign of judges, in half a verse. Mormon opens by correcting what the reader would expect from 3 Nephi 6:30.

phrases.term: They did separate one from another into tribes, every man according to his family and his kindred and friends
phrases.text: What replaced the government. When the national structure fails, people fall back on the smallest unit that still holds.

phrases.term: There was no man among them save he had much family and many kindreds and friends
phrases.text: Why the tribes came out large. Everyone was already inside a network, so the fracture ran along lines that already existed.

phrases.term: Like the dog to his vomit, or like the sow to her wallowing in the mire
phrases.text: Mormon quoting a proverb at his own people. 2 Peter 2:22 gives the same two images in the same order.

phrases.term: He was one of the chiefest who had given his voice against the prophets
phrases.text: The band's king identified by his record. He is known for what he said in the trials of 3 Nephi 6.

phrases.term: They were united in the hatred of those who had entered into a covenant to destroy the government
phrases.text: The tribes' only common ground. Mormon grants that they were not a righteous people and notes what held them together anyway.

phrases.term: They did establish very strict laws that one tribe should not trespass against another
phrases.text: Order rebuilt at the lowest level that works. It produces some peace and does nothing about the prophets being stoned.

phrases.term: Being eye-witness to their quick return from righteousness unto their wickedness
phrases.text: The second thing Nephi is an eye-witness of. The first is the ministry of Christ, and the two are named in the same breath.

phrases.term: A part of them would not suffice, therefore they are not written in this book
phrases.text: Mormon's reason for leaving material out. A fragment would misrepresent it, so he gives none.

phrases.term: Even his brother did he raise from the dead
phrases.text: Reported in six words with no elaboration. 3 Nephi 19:4 gives the brother's name as Timothy and places him among the twelve.

phrases.term: There were none who were brought unto repentance who were not baptized with water
phrases.text: Mormon stopping to make sure the reader notices. Verse 25 has Nephi ordaining men to perform it as a witness before God and the people.

verses.label: v. 5
verses.title: A collapse with no fighting in it
verses.text: The record inserts a fact that runs against expectation: "all this was done, and there were no wars as yet among them." The government has been destroyed, the population has sorted itself into tribes, and nobody has yet taken up arms. The cause given in the same verse is not violence but influence, "all this iniquity had come upon the people because they did yield themselves unto the power of Satan."

verses.label: v. 8
verses.title: A speed measured in years, and a borrowed simile
verses.text: The record states how fast the change happened and then compares it: "six years had not passed away since the more part of the people had turned from their righteousness, like the dog to his vomit, or like the sow to her wallowing in the mire." Both figures stand together at 2 Pet. 2:22, in the same order and applied to the same kind of relapse. The record supplies no attribution, and the number, six years, is the part a reader can check against 3 Nephi 1.

verses.label: v. 9–10
verses.title: A king identified by what he had done before
verses.text: The record names the man and then gives his qualification, and the qualification is a specific past act: "did place at their head a man whom they did call Jacob," and "he was one of the chiefest who had given his voice against the prophets who testified of Jesus." He is not described by strength, birth or wealth. What recommends him to the band is his record in the trials of 3 Nephi 6:21–23, and the record says so.

verses.label: v. 15–17
verses.title: A three-part reason for leaving material out
verses.text: The record explains an omission with an argument rather than an apology: "he did minister many things unto them; and all of them cannot be written, and a part of them would not suffice, therefore they are not written in this book." Three steps, and the middle one is the unusual part, since it rules out the obvious compromise of printing a selection. Having ruled out both the whole and the part, the record prints neither and moves on.

verses.label: v. 24–26
verses.title: The compiler stops the story to state a rule
verses.text: One verse breaks out of the narrative and addresses the reader directly: "Now I would have you to remember also, that there were none who were brought unto repentance who were not baptized with water." The tense changes and the subject becomes procedure. Verse 25 then reports the arrangement that made it possible, "there were ordained of Nephi, men unto this ministry, that all such as should come unto them should be baptized with water." A chapter about a collapsing state pauses over an administrative requirement.

chapter.title: The conspiracy fails at its stated aim
chapter.text: 3 Nephi 6:30 planned a king. Verse 1 reports that what they got was a murdered judge and no king at all.

chapter.title: Collapse is not the same as war
chapter.text: Verse 5 says there were no wars as yet. A country can lose its government while everyone stays home.

chapter.title: The tribes are the pre-existing structure
chapter.text: Verses 2 and 4 have people falling back on family and friendship. Nothing new is built; the older layer simply starts holding the weight again.

chapter.title: The unrighteous are capable of order
chapter.text: Verse 14 has them agreeing not to fight and passing strict laws. Mormon grants the competence and notes they stoned prophets anyway.

chapter.title: Six years is the measure
chapter.text: Verse 8 dates the whole reversal. The universal belief of 3 Nephi 5:1 was less than a decade earlier.

chapter.title: Nephi's authority is documented before it is used
chapter.text: Verse 15 lists angels, the voice, and eye-witness knowledge. The ministry follows the credentials.

chapter.title: Undeniable power did not persuade
chapter.text: Verse 18 says they could not disbelieve him, and verse 21 says few were converted. The record holds both.

chapter.title: Mormon interrupts to insist on baptism
chapter.text: Verse 24 is addressed to the reader. He wants no ambiguity about what accompanied repentance in this ministry.

applications.title: Notice what people fall back on
applications.text: When the government went, the tribes appeared instantly because they were already there. Whatever you would fall back on is worth strengthening now.

applications.title: Count the years honestly
applications.text: Six years covered the whole reversal. Decline that feels gradual from inside is usually faster than the people living through it believe.

applications.title: A coalition can run on hatred alone
applications.text: The tribes were not a righteous people, and the record says what held them together was hatred of the band that had destroyed the government. An alliance built only on a shared enemy lasts precisely as long as the enemy does.

applications.title: Order without repentance is still order
applications.text: They kept the peace between tribes and stoned the prophets. Do not read functioning arrangements as evidence that things are well.

applications.title: Some things do not survive excerpting
applications.text: Mormon writes that a part of Nephi's ministry would not suffice, so none of it goes into the book. Not everything can be sampled, and saying so is better than handing over a fragment that misrepresents the whole.

applications.title: Expect that being undeniable is not the same as being heeded
applications.text: They could not disbelieve him and mostly did not follow him. Winning the argument and changing the person are separate events.

applications.title: A demonstration can produce anger
applications.text: Nephi raised his brother from the dead where they could see it, and the people witnessed it and were angry at his power. Proving your case can worsen the other party's position without moving them off it.

applications.title: Ordain other people to do it
applications.text: Nephi ordained men to the ministry of baptism so that everyone who came could be received. When the demand for something you do exceeds you, the useful move is to make more people able to do it.

questions.text: Who is my tribe, and what would I do if larger structures failed?
What have I returned to that I thought I had left?
What am I united with others in hating?
Where have I settled for peace instead of repentance?
What am I actually an eye-witness of?
Whose truth have I resented rather than accepted?
What have I said I believed without doing the thing that goes with it?

entries.head: 3 Ne. 6:30

anchor.quote: they did not establish a king over the land

entries.reason: the covenant that planned exactly that, and failed at it

targets.quote: they did covenant one with another to destroy the governor, and to establish a king over the land,
targets.verse_text: And they did set at defiance the law and the rights of their country; and they did covenant one with another to destroy the governor, and to establish a king over the land, that the land should no more be at liberty but should be subject unto kings.
targets.markdown: And they did set at defiance the law and the rights of their country; and **they did covenant one with another to destroy the governor, and to establish a king over the land**, that the land should no more be at liberty but should be subject unto kings.

entries.head: 3 Ne. 6:23

anchor.quote: they did stone the prophets and did cast them out from among them

entries.reason: the earlier killings, done secretly to evade the governor

targets.quote: who were taken and put to death secretly by the judges,
targets.verse_text: Now there were many of those who testified of the things pertaining to Christ who testified boldly, who were taken and put to death secretly by the judges, that the knowledge of their death came not unto the governor of the land until after their death.
targets.markdown: Now there were many of those who testified of the things pertaining to Christ who testified boldly, **who were taken and put to death secretly by the judges**, that the knowledge of their death came not unto the governor of the land until after their death.

targets.markdown: Verily I say unto you, that whoso repenteth of his sins through your words, and desireth to be baptized in my name, on this wise shall ye baptize them—Behold, **ye shall go down and stand in the water, and in my name shall ye baptize them**.

anchor.quote: and even his brother did he raise from the dead, after he had been stoned and suffered death by the people

entries.head: 3 Ne. 9:9

anchor.quote: he was one of the chiefest who had given his voice against the prophets

entries.reason: the city named when it was burned

targets.quote: which was inhabited by the people of king Jacob,
targets.verse_text: And behold, that great city Jacobugath, which was inhabited by the people of king Jacob, have I caused to be burned with fire because of their sins and their wickedness, which was above all the wickedness of the whole earth, because of their secret murders and combinations; for it was they that did destroy the peace of my people and the government of the land; therefore I did cause them to be burned, to destroy them from before my face, that the blood of the prophets and the saints should not come up unto me any more against them.
targets.markdown: And behold, that great city Jacobugath, **which was inhabited by the people of king Jacob**, have I caused to be burned with fire because of their sins and their wickedness, which was above all the wickedness of the whole earth, because of their secret murders and combinations; for it was they that did destroy the peace of my people and the government of the land; therefore I did cause them to be burned, to destroy them from before my face, that the blood of the prophets and the saints should not come up unto me any more against them.

entries.head: Mosiah 29:26

anchor.quote: and thus they did destroy the government of the land

entries.reason: the rule government was to rest on, per Mosiah

targets.quote: law—to do your business by the voice of the people.
targets.verse_text: Now it is not common that the voice of the people desireth anything contrary to that which is right; but it is common for the lesser part of the people to desire that which is not right; therefore this shall ye observe and make it your law—to do your business by the voice of the people.
targets.markdown: Now it is not common that the voice of the people desireth anything contrary to that which is right; but it is common for the lesser part of the people to desire that which is not right; therefore this shall ye observe and make it your **law—to do your business by the voice of the people**.

anchor.quote: there were none who were brought unto repentance who were not baptized with water

entries.reason: Nephi arguing from the Lamb's own baptism to everyone else's

targets.verse_text: And now, if the Lamb of God, he being holy, should have need to be baptized by water, to fulfil all righteousness, O then, how much more need have we, being unholy, to be baptized, yea, even by water!
targets.markdown: And now, if the Lamb of God, he being holy, should have need to be baptized by water, to fulfil all righteousness, O then, **how much more need have we, being unholy, to be baptized, yea, even by water**!

entries.reason: the same gifts withdrawn from a later generation

targets.markdown: But wickedness did prevail upon the face of the whole land, insomuch that the Lord did take away his beloved disciples, and **the work of miracles and of healing did cease because of the iniquity of the people**.

entries.head: 2 Pet. 2:22

anchor.quote: like the dog to his vomit, or like the sow to her wallowing in the mire

entries.reason: the same proverb, same two animals, same order

targets.verse_text: But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.
targets.markdown: But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, **The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire**.
